evidence: Traupman 86: in the early evening, prīmā vesperā
terms.comment: Latin says “the first” of the period: prīmā lūce, early in the morning, at first light; prīmō vēre, early in spring; prīmā vesperā, early in the evening.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.97: ab ineunte aetāte, from early childhood (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The participle of ineō in an ablative absolute, “as the spring begins”; see at the beginning of the year.

phrases.latin: ineunte vēre … ea quae gemma dīcitur, ā quā oriēns ūva sē ostendit
phrases.english: early in spring … what is called the bud, from which the young grape shows itself
We’ll set off at first light tomorrow.

sources: Lewis & Short: primus · Lewis & Short: ineo
